newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOJ says monetary policy geared to ensure recovery.
newsitem.headline: BOJ says monetary policy geared to ensure recovery.

text.p: Japan's monetary policy will continue to put emphasis on ensuring a secure basis for economic recovery, Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Yasuo Matsushita told a meeting of securities firms on Thursday.

"For the time being, our monetary policy management will continue to put emphasis on securing a firm basis for economic recovery, while keeping careful watch over developments in monetary and economic conditions," Matsushita said.

He said Japan's economic recovery was continuing steadily but the pace was still gradual. For example, growth in industrial output remained gradual on the back of inventory adjustments in the semiconductor sector and some materials industries.
"It is necessary for the current economic recovery to strengthen further in order for it to move towards a firm self-sustainable recovery track," he said.
Although net exports are on a declining trend, public works spending and housing investment remain at high levels and consumer spending is gradually recovering.

A rebound in corporate capital spending, mainly among large firms, is slowly spreading to non-manufacturers and small and medium-sized firms. Drops in domestic prices are gradually coming to a halt, he said.
Matsushita also stressed the importance of carrying out deregulation and reforms for revitalising the private-sector economy.

He said it was becoming possible to act more quickly and efficiently in handling failures of financial institutions with the steady implementation of new government schemes to cope with Japan's problem loans.
He welcomed moves by companies that were making use of deregulation implemented since last year by actively raising funds through capital markets, especially in primary markets.

Matsushita said global standards must be taken into account in perfecting market infrastructure, such as abolishing unfair trade practices to protect investors, stepping up disclosures and fine-tuning distribution and settlement systems.

He said the BOJ would work with others who had made efforts to introduce a rolling settlement system for transactions in Japanese government bonds and those who had been working to improve the system of delivery and settlement of corporate bonds for a better market infrastructure.
